sop-from-memo.output:
```
WATER HEATER SWAP · Maple & Sons Plumbing

YOU WILL NEED
• Main water shutoff valve (at meter)
• Electrical breaker for heater
• Garden hose (from van)
• Floor drain access
• New flex lines (always)
• ASK OWNER: expansion tank policy when check valve is present on main line

STEPS
1. Shut the water at the main valve — do not rely on the local shutoff valve alone.
2. Kill the breaker for the heater at the panel.
3. Run a garden hose from the heater drain to the floor drain and drain completely.
4. Disconnect the old heater (inlet, outlet, flex lines).
5. Remove the old unit and haul to van.
6. Position the new heater in place.
7. Install new flex lines — use new lines every time, regardless of old line condition.
8. Fill the new heater from the main supply.
9. Bleed air at the closest faucet to the heater until water runs clear.
10. Restore power at the breaker.
11. Wait 20 minutes, then inspect all connections and the base for leaks.
12. Take a photo of the installed unit for the job file.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
• Water shut at main, breaker off, old unit drained and removed.
• New flex lines connected, unit filled and bled.
• Breaker back on, no leaks visible after 20 minutes.
• Photo in file.

COMMON MISTAKES & HOW TO CHECK
1. **Trusting the local valve instead of the main** → Check: the floor drain stays dry during draining; water stops flowing within 30 seconds of opening the drain valve.
2. **Powering up before bleeding air** → Check: you heard water run at the faucet for 10+ seconds; no sputtering or hissing at the heater after power is on.
3. **Missing the expansion tank when a check valve is on the main** → ASK OWNER whether this job requires expansion tank inspection or adjustment on every swap, or only in certain conditions.

---
_This draft is ready to share with new hires. Review for accuracy before posting._
```
